tagline: Back roads to the lick where the mammoths got stuck.
intro: From US 42 at Beaverlick, KY 338 heads west through Boone County to Big Bone, where the creek runs down to the Ohio. The byway goes on by Rabbit Hash and along KY 18 through Belleview to Woolper Road at Commissary Corner, about 20 miles in all.

The draw was always the springs. Mammoths are believed to have come for the salt around them, and the ground was soft enough that many animals stuck fast. In 1809 a salt works went up beside them, until it turned out the weak brine took 500 to 600 gallons of water to make a bushel. By 1812 it had failed.

moments.title: Beaverlick
moments.text: A fur trading site that grew to a hotel, a flour mill and three churches, and now keeps mostly its historic houses, churches and cemeteries.

moments.title: Big Bone Lick State Park
moments.text: Meriwether Lewis came for bones in 1803, and in 1807 William Clark carried off more than 300 for Jefferson, which helped naturalists tell a mastodon from a mammoth.

moments.title: Rabbit Hash
moments.text: Mail kept going astray to Carrollton, so the hamlet of Carlton became Rabbit Hash, and since 1998 it has elected dogs as its mayor.
